reason: Ten-move embodiment test on the 3D map showed the web_embody/web_move/web_turn/web_look tools have pitfalls no existing skill records: the body may have no figure (moves drive the person's mascot), address moves land short or overshoot, turns race the look, and web_look returns far too many entries. A future session driving these tools needs these checks up front.

The demo could not open a worker thread from its 2D figure until both events were dispatched. The 2D figure handler is repo-specific, so it belongs in this project skill, not the global Playwright one.

The follow-camera work found that an exponential ease fails the eased-move check, and the spring fix is the working approach. The drag threshold is a user-facing navigation rule the next session will need when touching follow.

During a seahorse tour the agent sent several acts in one batch, which cut each other off, and narrated a marker as red from ticket data when the picture showed a blue cube. The user then asked "you can see?". The navigation skill should carry the one-act-at-a-time rule and the look-before-describe rule.
The trigger missed tour, emote and narration requests on the 3D map, which is where this episode's mistakes happened. Widening the description lets the skill load for them.
Asked "you can see?", the agent first answered from act replies alone, then had to look and correct itself. The rule is to look first, then answer about sight.

The episode asked the seahorse to dance, come here, come close and ride a tour, but this skill was never loaded because its description names none of those words. Widening the trigger so the next such request loads it first.

Three facts this episode established that the skill lacks: the valid emote list, a dance is a sequence of acts, web_come to view lands far when zoomed out, and a web_come must be ended before a manual move. A restart mid-act was also seen; the retry worked.
